svg.title: A nurse discovers a loop of umbilical cord protruding from a laboring client's vagina. Which actions should the nurse take immediately?
svg.desc: Cord prolapse is an obstetric emergency: the nurse calls for help while staying with the client, uses gloved fingers to lift the presenting part off the cord to relieve compression, positions the client knee-chest or Trendelenburg with a hip roll, and gives oxygen while preparing for emergent birth. The cord should never be pushed back into the vagina, since this can worsen compression and raise infection risk, and fundal pressure could force the presenting part further onto the cord instead of relieving it.
